The '''Rim Faction''', led by [[Orn Free Taa/Legends|Orn Free Taa]], was one of the two major factions of [[Senator/Legends|senators]] and [[Junior Representative/Legends|representatives]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] during the last years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Majority of its membership were predominantly from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. The faction included [[Mot-Not Rab/Legends|Mot-Not Rab]], [[Tikkes/Legends|Tikkes]], and [[Onaconda Farr/Legends|Onaconda Farr]].

==Formation and beliefs==
Most of the [[Rim]] Faction's members were [[Alien/Legends|non-Human]], and [[Astrography|astrographically]], most came from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] as well as the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]], and also the various special interest groups&mdash;such as the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]], [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]], [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]], and [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]].

They were a politically conservative faction and so advocated reducing the power and influence of the Republic government. As such, they commonly stood for the maximization of planetary sovereignty, placing them in direct opposition to the [[Core Faction/Legends|Core Faction]], who favored greater centralization of power. Fiscally, the Rim Faction advocated for economic liberalism, thus supporting free trade, low taxes, minimal restrictions on enterprise, and the deregulation of markets.

==History==
The Rim Faction were strong opponents of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]], and were quick to seize upon his weakness in the aftermath of the [[Eriadu Trade Summit]] disaster of [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]]. In the hope of restricting his ability to pass legislation unfavorable to them, Taa directed the Rim Faction to elect [[Mas Amedda/Legends|Mas Amedda]], one of their own, into the powerful position of [[Vice Chair/Legends|Vice Chair]].

The [[32 BBY/Legends|next year]], it was the strong support of the Rim Faction for Amidala's [[Vote of No Confidence/Legends|vote of no confidence]] that enabled the toppling of Valorum and the [[Supreme Chancellor election, 32 BBY/Legends|ensuing election for Chancellor]]. Once more on the nomination of Taa, [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], despite being independent of any Senate political grouping, was the Rim Faction's nominee for Chancellor. It is possible that because of his neutrality, a rogue section of the Rim Faction backed [[Ainlee Teem/Legends|Ainlee Teem]] for Chancellor. However, Palpatine won.

Taa's hope that Palpatine could be controlled, or at least counted on to not be a nuisance, were eventually realized as false when he ensured the [[Core Faction/Legends|Core Faction]]'s attachment to him. During the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] and [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a large number of the Rim Faction's membership seceded and joined the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], either voluntarily or were expelled from the Senate. Other Rim Faction senators, such as Taa, [[Aks Moe/Legends|Aks Moe]], and [[Onaconda Farr/Legends|Onaconda Farr]], supported the [[Military Creation Act/Legends|Military Creation Act]] vigorously. Despite the continued loyalty of Taa and Amedda, this combined with Palpatine's courting of the Core faction resulted in great weakening of the Rim Faction.
